cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus asks if Peter loves Him more than these. Jesus says, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?” (John 21:15). The passage doesn't spell out what “these” means, so I'll leave it open too. Simon Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, hears this once breakfast is over. I think a question that short and that direct makes a man stand up straight.

The answer is True. After Peter answers the second time, Jesus tells him, “Shepherd My sheep.” (John 21:16). Peter gets another job, not a lecture, friends. I think that tells you something about how Jesus handles a man who says he loves Him: He gives him something to do.

The word is hurt. The text says Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “…do you love Me…” (John 21:17). Peter doesn't storm off, though. He answers, “Lord, You know all things…” and, “You know I love You.”

The answer is where he does not want to go. Jesus says someone else will dress Peter and lead him “…where you do not want to go.” (John 21:18). It's a quiet line with a lot packed in. Jesus says that when Peter was young, he dressed himself and walked where he wanted. I think this is one of the heavier parts of the passage, so let's take it slow.

The answer is True. The writer explains that Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God (John 21:19). We're told right there what the words are pointing to. It's a heavy thing to hear, friends, and I won't joke about it. Then Jesus says to Peter, “Follow Me.”

The word is follow. After Jesus finishes, He tells Peter, “Follow Me.” (John 21:19). Short and simple, with no speech attached. Jesus uses the same two words again a few verses later, and I'll get to that when we meet them.

What Peter asks is, “Lord, what about him?” (John 21:21). He turns around, spots the disciple whom Jesus loved, and the question just comes out. I think we've all done that, glancing at the next person's plate when we should look at our own. Jesus answers him directly, and that answer is coming up.

The word is die. The rumor spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die (John 21:23). The brothers here are fellow believers. The rumor grew out of Jesus' answer, and the text sets it straight right away. Rumors move like cookie crumbs, friends: one bump of the counter and they're everywhere.

The answer is False. The text says plainly that Jesus did not say this disciple would not die. He said only, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you?” (John 21:22-23). Notice the “if” in His words. It's a small word, but it's holding up that whole sentence.

The answer is the disciple whom Jesus loved. John 21:24 says, “This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who has written them down.” That's the same disciple Peter turned around and saw following them. Then the passage adds, “And we know that his testimony is true.” He wrote it all down, friends, and the rumor corrected itself right on the page.
